subject: Temporary throughput bridge & reserved GPU behavior — AtlasPay
messages:
From: Eleni Marcos <eleni@atlaspay.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-26T09:15:00Z
Subject: Request: temporary throughput guarantee while we ramp

Hi Soojin,

Quick background: AtlasPay will be onboarding our fraud-scoring ingestion to Redwood Dedicated the week of Sep 6. Our initial traffic is expected to be small but will spike as we roll out to production consumers on Sep 20 (projected token throughput increase ~5x over two weeks). Procurement asked us to secure a short-term throughput commitment for the first 30 days post-prod to avoid missed SLAs for our customers.

Specifically we are looking for: a) guaranteed average concurrent token throughput of 1.2M tokens/min for 30 days after Sep 20, b) reserved access to an additional 2 GPUs from the same dedicated pool if queueing exceeds our threshold, and c) a simple credit formula if we see tail latency > 800ms P95.

Can Redwood provide a temporary addendum or a bridging clause to your standard Dedicated SLA? We are ready to sign an addendum and route it through our procurement legal today if we can agree on the parameters.

Thanks,
Eleni
Procurement, AtlasPay

---
Attachment: none

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Eleni Marcos <eleni@atlaspay.com>, AtlasPay Procurement <procurement@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2027-08-26T12:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput guarantee while we ramp

Eleni — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support a short-term throughput bridge but need to lock a few operational details before I send a formal addendum.

Proposed next steps:
- I will circulate a draft temporary throughput bridge with clear start/end dates and an explicit preemption/queueing behavior table.
- If you can share the expected traffic profile (peaks per hour, typical sequence length), our capacity team will confirm whether the "+2 reserved GPU" is the right construct or whether a burst token pool is safer.
- We usually define latency credits on a % of calls impacted or by P95/P99 bands — I will include both options.

I have looped in Ben (sales ops) and Lauren (account lead) to align on commercial terms. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben / Lauren — forwarding AtlasPay request. Key commercial asks: 30-day temporary guarantee, +2 reserved GPUs (or equivalent burst pool), and a credit if P95 > 800ms.

1) Ben: is a short-term reserved GPU carveout feasible pricing-wise? We can offer a "temporary reserved burst" at a fixed daily rate + lower unit price on the bridged capacity.
2) Lauren: if we approve, do you want this to live as an SLA addendum or as an internal SOW attached to the master services agreement? Procurement prefers an addendum they can attach to DocuSign.

I'll draft the operational table (start/end dates, preemption rules, queue thresholds). We should keep the language narrow and timebound.

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-27T10:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasPay throughput bridge — need ops/legal posture

Quick take: feasible. Two options to present — prefer we give both so Procurement can choose.

Option A — Reserved GPU carveout (explicit, easier to reason about)
- +2 reserved GPUs allocated from the customer's dedicated pool for a 30-day window.
- Price: $1,200/day for the window (one-time daily fee).
- Preemption: these GPUs are soft-reserved — they may be preempted for platform-wide emergencies with 4-hour notice; during preemption, AtlasPay receives a token-based credit per degraded minute.

Option B — Burst token pool (operationally simpler)
- A burst pool capacity defined as X tokens/min (we will map to expected concurrency).
- Price: one-time provisioning fee + per-token surcharge during the 30-day window.
- No preemption but subject to provider-scope throttling when the entire region is saturated.

Latency credits: propose a tiered credit: P95 801–1200ms => 5% credit on monthly Dedicated fee; P95 >1200ms => 15% credit. Credits capped at 30% of monthly dedicated fee.

I will attach a draft SLA table (SLA_Table_ATLAS_vs_STD.xlsx) and create the PDF addendum for signatures. Lauren — if Procurement insists on DocuSign addendum, we'll push the PDF there.

Ben
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Table_ATLAS_vs_STD.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Eleni Marcos <eleni@atlaspay.com>, AtlasPay Procurement <procurement@atlaspay.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-28T15:20:00Z
Subject: Draft: Temporary throughput bridge (30-day) — AtlasPay (attached)

Hi Eleni — please find attached a draft PDF of the temporary throughput bridge and an XLS that maps the proposed commitments to our standard Dedicated SLA. Highlights:
- Term: 30 days starting on the production ramp date (you confirm production go-live date in writing).
- Throughput: guaranteed average throughput of 1.2M tokens/min (measured as 15-minute rolling average) for the 30-day window.
- Burst capacity: we propose Option A (soft-reserved +2 GPUs) priced at $1,200/day. Option B (burst token pool) is included as an alternate with pricing examples.
- Queueing behavior: reserved GPUs are prioritized for AtlasPay requests up to the guaranteed throughput; if queueing exceeds the threshold (10s queue depth average over a 5-minute window), preemption protections kick in as defined.
- Latency credits: tiered P95 credit (5% / 15%), capped at 30% of monthly Dedicated fee.

Next steps: please confirm which option you prefer and the official production ramp date. If you approve, we will upload the PDF to DocuSign and target signature within 48 hours to ensure provisioning completes ahead of Sep 6.

Attached:
- 20270828_TempThroughputBridge_Draft.pdf (proposed language)
- SLA_Table_ATLAS_vs_STD.xlsx (mapping table)

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

All — thanks, this looks good and mostly aligns to our needs. Two quick asks before we sign:
1) Can the P95 credit threshold be referenced to our tagged service (so we don't get credits from unrelated testing traffic)? We can provide the service tags.
2) For preemption notice, can we change "4-hour notice" to "2-hour notice" for soft-reserved GPUs? That shorter runway helps our SREs reroute ephemeral pipelines.

If you can accept those two tweaks, we'll approve and route the addendum. Otherwise we may ask legal for a final redline which will add delay.

Best,
Eleni
Procurement, AtlasPay
